slides.headline: SHE CALLED IT SILLY. FOUR YEARS LATER IT OUTLIVED THE FRANCHISE
slides.image_prompt: Graphics tablet on plain desk, screen facing away, outlasting the franchise that once dismissed it

caption:
She called her Pokemon fan art silly. Four years later, nothing has topped it. 🎨

Four years ago, kianamaiart posted a piece of Team Rocket fan art. She didn't hype it up. She didn't call it her best work. She called it silly.

It spread anyway. Then kept spreading. The kind of quiet sharing that happens when something lands without trying to.

Now it sits so deep in Pokemon culture that fans hold new releases up against it. The official franchise. Measured against one fan's throwaway afternoon.

Her post asking whether anything would ever top it got 39,000 likes. Because everyone who has ever made something small and dismissed it before anyone else could see it felt that.

She called it silly and posted it. Four years later, it's still the one. Send this to someone sitting on a draft they've convinced themselves isn't ready.

Thousands of creators talk themselves out of posting something they call silly every single day. Most never find out what they had. The ones who hit publish do.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

pinned_comment: Four years is a long time on the internet. Most things last four weeks. The one she called silly is still the measuring stick.
